title: Capstone: a local expense reporter
subtitle: Connect reading, validation, calculation, and display to build an expense summary tool.
concept: Connect reading, validation, calculation, and display to build an expense summary tool.
intuition: Read the bill, validate amounts, total them by category, then display a report.
objectives: Start with a bill you can check by hand

body.title: Start with a bill you can check by hand
body.text: Take food at 125 cents, transport at 200, and food at 75. Calculate independently: food totals 200, transport 200, and the grand total is 400 cents. Start with three in-memory records, combining Chapter 3 lists and dictionaries with Chapter 4 functions. Do not add files, command-line parsing, and tests all at once.

body.title: Separate four responsibilities
body.text: First read CSV (Section 5.2). Second validate columns, category, and integer-cent amounts, rejecting zero and negatives (Section 4.4). Third accumulate amounts by category in a dictionary (Section 3.2). Fourth display results in a stable order. Verify the accumulation before connecting file input. The appendix provides complete source with a function for each responsibility.

body.title: Add the command-line interface last
body.text: Save the appendix source and sample.csv in one folder and enter it in a terminal. Run python3 expense_report.py --help to check usage, then python3 expense_report.py sample.csv. Store amounts as integer cents and convert to currency units only for display. A CLI accepts arguments through terminal commands; argparse reads the filename. The class declarations in the full tests organize unittest cases; object-oriented mechanisms belong in a later course.

formalDefinition.text: The reporter separates reading, validation, aggregation, and display. Each record must contain a positive integer amount in cents.
conditions: Reject zero or negative amounts, missing columns, empty categories, and malformed amounts. Each record uses positive integer cents.
No records gives a total of 0. That differs from an invalid record whose amount is 0.

derivation.text: Each record is a dictionary containing category and amount.
For a category's first occurrence, start its total at 0.
Food totals 125 + 75 and transport 200, for a grand total of 400.

workedExamples.title: Build the aggregation core
workedExamples.problem: Sum three small records by category. Assume the records have already been validated and contain positive integer cents.
steps: Each record is a dictionary containing category and amount.
For a category's first occurrence, start its total at 0.
Food totals 125 + 75 and transport 200, for a grand total of 400.

answer.code:
records = [
    {"category": "food", "amount": 125},
    {"category": "transport", "amount": 200},
    {"category": "food", "amount": 75},
]
totals = {}
total = 0
for record in records:
    category = record["category"]
    amount = record["amount"]
    totals[category] = totals.get(category, 0) + amount
    total = total + amount
print(totals["food"])
print(totals["transport"])
print(total)

workedExamples.title: Convert units only for display
steps: Compute the total using integer cents.
Divide by 100 to convert cents to currency units.
In the f-string, :.2f displays two decimal places. The internal accounts still use integer cents.

commonMistakes.claim: Every amount convertible to an integer belongs in the bill.
commonMistakes.correction: Each amount must also exceed 0. This project rejects zero and negative records.
Report the error so the user can correct it rather than hiding a data problem.

learningCheck.question: How should the tool handle a negative amount under this project's rules?
choices: Add it because arithmetic is possible
Explain the error and reject the input
learningCheck.explanation: Each record must contain positive integer cents. Reject zero and negatives explicitly.
feedback: Being usable in arithmetic does not satisfy the input requirements.
Silently changing values hides the original data problem behind an apparently successful report.
